text: MitosisEngine has no negative feedback from population size to tension — the split loop is positively self-reinforcing. Measured: mean tension per cell rises 0.0315 (3 cells) -> 0.3881 (32 cells), 12x, because children inherit parent weights plus noise so outputs grow so tension grows so the split condition holds harder the more it has fired. Consequence: with the mean-window criterion (ce09ead) division works under varying input but there is no usable band — bar 0.0462 gives the 32 ceiling, 0.0594 gives the 2 floor, nothing between. At the shipped noise_scale=0.014, 97% of splits are undone by merges (984 splits / 955 merges); raising noise stops the churn and saturates immediately instead. A working population needs division to lower per-cell load, or the trigger to normalise by population size — either changes what tension MEANS, so it is an owner decision. Measured in docs/mitosis-calibration.md.
